issues.sym: Shuddering or jerking when pulling away from a stop, hesitation, slipping, or fluid leaking near the clutch housing.
issues.why: This automatic uses dry clutches like a manual. Leaking input shaft seals contaminate the clutches and worn clutches grab unevenly. Ford extended warranty coverage and a class action settlement followed.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer inspect the clutches, seals, and software. Check whether your VIN still has extended transmission coverage.

issues.sym: The car drops into neutral or loses drive while moving, will not start or go into gear, or shows a transmission warning.
issues.why: The transmission control module mounted on the gearbox can fail, often from heat or moisture. Ford extended coverage for this module.
issues.next: Treat loss of drive as a safety issue. Have the module tested and check your VIN for extended coverage and reprogramming campaigns.

issues.t: Stalling after refueling or crushed fuel tank
issues.sym: Stalling or rough running, especially right after filling up, a fuel gauge that reads wrong, or a check engine light for the evaporative system.
issues.why: A stuck-open canister purge valve can pull too much vacuum on the fuel tank and deform it. Ford recalled these cars to replace the valve and check the tank.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the purge valve recall. A shop can confirm the codes and inspect the tank.

issues.t: Door won't latch or bounces open
issues.sym: A door-ajar warning while driving, or a door that will not stay closed.
issues.why: A part inside the door latch can wear and stop catching. Ford recalled the latches and later expanded the campaign.
issues.next: Do not drive with a door that will not latch. Check your VIN for open door latch recalls.

issues.t: Valve seat can drop into the cylinder
issues.sym: A sudden loud knocking or clattering, a hard misfire, heavy shaking and loss of power, often with no warning beforehand.
issues.why: On the base single-cam engine, a pressed-in valve seat in the cylinder head can work loose and fall into the cylinder, where it gets hammered by the piston. Overheating makes it more likely.
issues.next: Shut the engine off right away if this happens; running it does more damage. Never let this engine overheat, and have any misfire checked promptly.

issues.t: Key will not turn in the ignition
issues.sym: The key goes in but will not turn, or it sticks and will not come back out. It tends to get worse until the car cannot be started.
issues.why: The small tumblers inside the ignition lock cylinder wear and jam.
issues.next: Do not force the key, which can break it off. Have the lock cylinder replaced before it leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Engine vibration from a worn top engine mount
issues.sym: Strong vibration through the steering wheel, seats and dash at idle or in gear at a stop, sometimes with a thump when you pull away.
issues.why: The upper engine mount on the passenger side wears out or its fluid-filled center leaks, so engine shake passes straight into the body.
issues.next: Have the engine mounts inspected. It is not an emergency, but a failed mount puts extra strain on the other mounts and the exhaust.

issues.t: Rear wheel bearings wear out early
issues.sym: A humming or rumbling from the back of the car that gets louder with speed.
issues.why: The rear wheel bearings on early cars can wear sooner than expected. Federal safety regulators opened an inquiry into them.
issues.next: Have the rear bearings checked for play and noise. Do not ignore a growling bearing for long, since a badly worn one can loosen the wheel.

issues.t: Rear door may not latch fully and can open (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door that needs slamming, sits slightly proud, or pops open while driving.
issues.why: The rear door latches can fail to catch completely, so the door looks closed but is not secure. Ford recalled the latches.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Do not carry rear passengers next to a door that does not latch firmly.

issues.t: Clogged in-tank fuel filter can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hesitation, surging and loss of power, worse in hot weather or with a low tank, and eventually stalling.
issues.why: The filter on the fuel pump module inside the tank can plug up and starve the engine of fuel. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the engine has started cutting out, have it fixed before driving in traffic.

issues.t: Battery cables can short and overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A check engine light, a no-start, a hot plastic smell, or smoke and melted wiring near the battery.
issues.why: The battery cables can rub through and short circuit, which can overheat the wiring and start a fire. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If you see smoke or smell melting plastic, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Rear wheel hub nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or a wobble from a rear wheel.
issues.why: On some early cars the nuts holding the rear hubs were not secure, which could let a rear wheel come loose. Ford recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have any rear wheel looseness inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Cruise control cable can hold the throttle open (recalls)
issues.sym: The engine keeps pulling after you lift off the gas pedal, so the car does not slow down as expected.
issues.why: The cruise control cable can snag and stop the throttle from closing fully. Ford ran two recalls on it.
issues.next: If it happens, brake firmly, shift to Neutral and pull over. Check your VIN for these recalls.

issues.t: Front suspension pinch bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Noise and vibration from the front end over bumps or when turning.
issues.why: The pinch bolts that clamp the front ball joints may not stay tight. Left alone, the joint can come apart or the ball joint stud can break. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have front-end clunks inspected promptly.
